A gorgeous voxel masterpiece held hostage by bot farms, server lag, and desperate developers.

Trove is, without a doubt, one of the most uniquely charming voxel MMORPGs ever created. At its core, it is an absolute blast—a vibrant, blocky sandbox that perfectly marries the boundless creativity of Minecraft with the frantic, loot-heavy dungeon crawling of Diablo. Choosing a class like the Neon Ninja or the Dino Tamer and blasting through procedurally generated realms to smash bosses and collect spectacular mounts is incredibly satisfying. When you couple that with the ability to build massive Club Worlds with your friends and customize your personal Cornerstone house, it's easy to see why so many of us fell head over heels in love with this game during its golden era.

However, if you look at the recent reviews, it is heartbreakingly clear that the game is in a massive downward spiral. The servers have become an absolute joke, plagued by a permanent, rubber-banding lag that teleports you backward every time you try to jump or execute a combo. Worse yet, the in-game economy has been completely obliterated by rampant bot farms and duplication exploits. Instead of aggressively fixing these fundamental engine and security issues, the development team’s baffling "solution" was to straight-up remove the player trading system, essentially alienating the core community. Rather than repairing a sinking ship, they continue to just stack event upon event, pretending everything is fine while the structural integrity of the game crumbles.

The tragedy of Trove is that beneath the aggressive pay-to-win microtransactions, the abysmally time-gated endgame gem grind, and the current technical disaster, there is still the skeleton of a 10/10 game. It is easily the best pixel MMO out there, but it is currently being choked to death by years of poor management and predatory monetization. If you are a veteran returning for nostalgia, prepare to be hit with profound disappointment; if you…

claims.claim: The game requires extensive grinding and repetition of tasks for gear and progression.

citations.review_text:
Pros
* It is a lot like Minecraft with its blocky, voxel-based worlds and building mechanics.
* Completely free to play without a mandatory purchase price.
* Action combat featuring distinct classes like knights, mages, and gunslingers.
* Hub worlds and portals that make it easy to jump into fast dungeons and adventures with others.
* Supports massive multiplayer environments with shared hub worlds and trading marketplaces.
* Includes open-world exploration, mounts, and fully customizable player housing.

Cons
* Heavy microtransactions and pay-to-progress elements can slow down free players.
* Grindy gameplay requires repeating the same tasks to level up gear.
* Server lag and stability issues can happen during busy times.

How Trove Compares to Minecraft
* Focus: Trove is an RPG focused on questing, dungeons, and loot, while Minecraft is a sandbox focused on survival, crafting, and building.
* Combat: Trove has fast, class-based action combat with abilities; Minecraft has simpler, real-time weapon swinging and archery.
* Economy: Trove features a player marketplace and trading system, whereas Minecraft relies entirely on gathering your own materials or trading with villagers.
* World Structure: Trove features massive, procedurally generated open worlds with building zones; Minecraft Dungeons uses fixed, linear levels selected from a mission map.
* Building Mechanics: Trove allows you to build and carry a personal house (Cornerstone) anywhere; Minecraft Dungeons has zero building or mining mechanics

Trove, developed and published by gamigo US Inc., is a free-to-play voxel-based MMORPG that combines the structure of a loot-driven online RPG with the creativity and accessibility of a sandbox building game. Set across a sprawling multiverse of procedurally generated worlds, it invites players to explore, fight, gather resources, and construct their own creations in an environment that feels both playful and expansive. Its blocky aesthetic immediately draws comparisons to sandbox staples, but beneath that familiar look lies a game heavily centered on progression, collection, and cooperative adventuring.

At the heart of Trove is its class system, which offers a wide variety of distinct characters, each with their own abilities and combat style. Players can unlock and switch between these classes freely once obtained, allowing for a flexible approach to gameplay. Some classes emphasize close-range combat, others rely on ranged attacks or magic, and a few lean into more unconventional mechanics. This variety helps keep the gameplay fresh, especially during the early and mid-game, as experimenting with different playstyles is both encouraged and rewarding. Combat itself is fast and arcade-like, focusing more on movement and quick reactions than on complex skill rotations, which makes it easy to pick up but somewhat limited in long-term depth.

Exploration plays a major role in shaping the overall experience. The game is divided into numerous biomes, each procedurally generated and filled with dungeons, enemies, and treasures to uncover. Players travel between these worlds through a central hub, gradually unlocking access to more challenging areas as their power increases. This constant sense of forward movement is one of Trove’s strengths, as there is always another world to visit or a tougher challenge to pursue. claims.claim: Reviewers report that endgame progression involves a very long and time-gated grind, particularly when upgrading items or attempting to acquire specific gear and classes.

citations.review_text:
While I do love this game in some aspects there is just too many cons then pros.
1. The game is very p2w focused & while yes you can gain a majority of the classes, equipment, materials & etc. through gameplay it is a grind & a half in order to achieve it esspecially with later game content.

2. After a while of gameplay doing the same things over & over again such as daily quests, dungeons & other grinds it can get extremely boring & mind numbing causing quite a bit of burnout as a result which is never a good thing when a game that is supose to be an escape from your 9-5 as a result becomes just as tedious & boring.

Overall there are alot of other sketchy things that might rub you the wrong way about the game but if you are that much of a die hard grinding fan then maybe you will feel right at home. The game does offer quite a bit of options for builds, classes & various other tools to give you a unique experience. The game also offers a huge amount of creativity for building such as transparent, glowing & various other blocks to get your builds just right.

Personally I would not reccommend it to anyone the grinding after a while just gets too tedious after a while esspecially once you make it towards the Geode Topside & the Light mechanic.

I've spent a lot of time playing this game, and I can honestly say it's one of the most addictive games I've played. The early and mid-game are genuinely fun, and the progression feels rewarding. If you really get into it, you'll probably find yourself logging in every single day because there's always something to do.

In the end game, Progression becomes painfully slow. Upgrading even a single item takes an unreasonable amount of time. For example, upgrading just one Mystic Gem to level 35 can take weeks, simply because you only receive one Ninth Life per week. Instead of feeling rewarding, the grind starts to feel like waiting for time-gated resources rather than actually playing the game.

Another major issue is the lack of updates. There haven't been any meaningful performance improvements in years, and bug fixes have also been almost nonexistent for years. It's disappointing because the game has a lot of potential, but it feels like it's been left behind. Long-standing performance issues and bugs remain, making the experience less enjoyable than it could be.

Overall, I still think the game is fun and incredibly addictive. The core gameplay is solid, and it's easy to understand why so many people stick with it. However, the end-game progression desperately needs to be rebalanced, and the developers really need to start releasing performance optimizations and bug-fix updates again.

I want to recommend this game because I genuinely enjoyed it, but in its current state, the end-game grind and lack of support make it difficult to do so.

If you'd like to see how this game has declined over the years, continue reading. If not, have a good day.

I've been playing since the beginning, before the Megalithic update released in 2017. This game used to be great! With a fun gameplay loop of grinding dungeons, getting gear, and the endgame grind of dragon souls. As time went on, it was getting better! Up until around the time when Trion worlds went under, and Gamigo took the game. Since then, Grinds have gotten more long and arduous. Getting to max power rank requires multiple hundreds of hours across months with plenty of rng stacked on top of time limited resources. This was fine for a while, since it was the only thing and kept people coming back. Then the vanguard came out. and the bard. and the solarian. All classes with entirely unique ways of obtaining them, and all nigh impossible to obtain for F2P players. It was abysmal. But I continued playing, because despite those disappointing classes, the game was still fun. But over the years, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ decisions have begun to plague this game. Things like crystal 4 and 5 weapons being impossible to obtain upon release, and now being trivial to obtain through power creep. citations.review_text:
While I do love this game in some aspects there is just too many cons then pros.
1. The game is very p2w focused & while yes you can gain a majority of the classes, equipment, materials & etc. through gameplay it is a grind & a half in order to achieve it esspecially with later game content.

2. After a while of gameplay doing the same things over & over again such as daily quests, dungeons & other grinds it can get extremely boring & mind numbing causing quite a bit of burnout as a result which is never a good thing when a game that is supose to be an escape from your 9-5 as a result becomes just as tedious & boring.

Overall there are alot of other sketchy things that might rub you the wrong way about the game but if you are that much of a die hard grinding fan then maybe you will feel right at home. The game does offer quite a bit of options for builds, classes & various other tools to give you a unique experience. The game also offers a huge amount of creativity for building such as transparent, glowing & various other blocks to get your builds just right.

Personally I would not reccommend it to anyone the grinding after a while just gets too tedious after a while esspecially once you make it towards the Geode Topside & the Light mechanic.

I've spent a lot of time playing this game, and I can honestly say it's one of the most addictive games I've played. The early and mid-game are genuinely fun, and the progression feels rewarding. If you really get into it, you'll probably find yourself logging in every single day because there's always something to do.

In the end game, Progression becomes painfully slow. Upgrading even a single item takes an unreasonable amount of time. For example, upgrading just one Mystic Gem to level 35 can take weeks, simply because you only receive one Ninth Life per week. Instead of feeling rewarding, the grind starts to feel like waiting for time-gated resources rather than actually playing the game.

Another major issue is the lack of updates. There haven't been any meaningful performance improvements in years, and bug fixes have also been almost nonexistent for years. It's disappointing because the game has a lot of potential, but it feels like it's been left behind. Long-standing performance issues and bugs remain, making the experience less enjoyable than it could be.

Overall, I still think the game is fun and incredibly addictive. The core gameplay is solid, and it's easy to understand why so many people stick with it. However, the end-game progression desperately needs to be rebalanced, and the developers really need to start releasing performance optimizations and bug-fix updates again.

I want to recommend this game because I genuinely enjoyed it, but in its current state, the end-game grind and lack of support make it difficult to do so.

Long time player here, uninstall this game. This game now installs an invasive third party anticheat, from an unknown Korean company (which, could be and probably is stealing your data) that can break your computer and can only be removed by editing your registry. Multiple people in the community have been reporting numerous computer issues after the update introducing it, even with the game off.

If you'd like to see how this game has declined over the years, continue reading. If not, have a good day.

I've been playing since the beginning, before the Megalithic update released in 2017. This game used to be great! With a fun gameplay loop of grinding dungeons, getting gear, and the endgame grind of dragon souls. As time went on, it was getting better! Up until around the time when Trion worlds went under, and Gamigo took the game. Since then, Grinds have gotten more long and arduous. Getting to max power rank requires multiple hundreds of hours across months with plenty of rng stacked on top of time limited resources. This was fine for a while, since it was the only thing and kept people coming back. Then the vanguard came out. and the bard. and the solarian. All classes with entirely unique ways of obtaining them, and all nigh impossible to obtain for F2P players. It was abysmal. But I continued playing, because despite those disappointing classes, the game was still fun. But over the years, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ decisions have begun to plague this game. Things like crystal 4 and 5 weapons being impossible to obtain upon release, and now being trivial to obtain through power creep. Mystic gear is completely out of the ballpark unless you no-life the game. The titles update is useless. The martial arts skill is useless. The potion bench whateverthehell is confusing and borderline useless. There are entire skill trees that make no sense to exist where they do. Everything's become a powercreep mess that pushes people to buy things to keep the game making money. No rebalancing u…

Unlike a lot of other old players, I'm not in the boat of "Oh this game used to be good". This game was never "good". Ever since the acquisition by Gamigo, this game was on a downhill trajectory. New classes becoming impossible to craft beginning with the Vanguardian update, having Delves introduced, and more monetization. This game is already dead. If you value your time and have enough self-respect, don't play this game. 
The Pros:
- Addictive(?) grinding system
- Unique and various classes
- Somewhat fun gameplay 
- Really nice building mechanics
The Cons:
- Microtransactions everywhere
- Extremely long grind to get to end-game
- Horrible management from Gamigo
- This game will die no matter what we do
I really really want Trove to at least somewhat succeed. I have been playing this game since 2017, with most of my hours on the Glyph launcher. But I cannot for literally any reason recommend anyone play this game.

Initially, I chose this game to play with my son and quickly got addicted. For me, it hit all MY checkmarks of what i like in an rpg: lots of character classes (x18), cool skins, fun, early, mid, endgame. Sure, the game is a grind, but that was to be expected in an F2P game. Trove isn't really Pay2Win, it's more like Pay2Win more. You have access to ALL the content as an F2P. 

Furthermore, after a week of playing as an F2P, I won all these in-game community awards and was given pay2win chests!!! I mean, here's devs that really appreciate their community. Next, the devs allow players to vote on what special gimmick will happen the following week. Next, the community is basically AWESOME. 99% of people help newbies with tips, etc. Every community has those 1% trolls; how to kill a troll: set them on fire XD

I did end up spending $$, but i'm happy with my purchases. For $7 you get a dragon, a character class, & other cool stuff.

The cons, i would say, are that when starting Trove, you've got TEN years of predecessor content which is 300% overwhelming. Then, they don't give you hardly any clues on specific tutorial people to find (the hubs are vast). That was very frustrating & had me yelling at the devs, lol. Also, the game frequently disconnects about once every 2-hours, but you can instantly go back to the area that you left--even amidst enemies. Lastly, when making a financial transaction, it takes anywhere from instantly to about 15 minutes for your purchase to arrive and instant paranoia kicks in if its late.

All in all, i give this game a PERFECT 10.0 because it hits ALL of my buttons. I'm a Pirate summoner class & I summon parrot cannoneers. How cute/cool is that?!

A rollercoaster of emotion this game. Either servers are broken and completely down because someone was mass teleporting people or it's working so fine that every single shot you shoot lands perfectly and feels SO good. Whatever the case. Whenever you play it. Whatever is happening. The game is in fact a game. One that's addicting so be prepared to not quit and just wait for the bad to be over so you can play freely again. I enjoy the game, but I also hate it in the ways were game should just game. You know what I mean?
